verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {applicant_name}, aged about {applicant_age} years, resident of {applicant_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above application are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

promptInstructions: Draft an application for maintenance under Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
CRITICAL: Use Section 144 BNSS — never refer to Section 125 CrPC. BNSS replaced CrPC effective 1 July 2024.

Plead applicant's capacity clearly (wife / divorced wife not remarried / minor legitimate child / minor illegitimate child / major child unable due to physical or mental abnormality / father or mother unable to maintain self).

For WIFE: plead valid marriage. Include negative averment that wife is not living in adultery, has not refused without sufficient reason to live with husband, and parties are not living separately by mutual consent (S.144(4) BNSS).
Plead respondent's sufficient means: occupation, monthly income, assets. Attach salary slips / bank statements / business records / property documents where available.
Plead specific instances of refusal or neglect to maintain.
Plead applicant's inability to maintain self — no income / insufficient income, dependent children, illness, etc.
Quantum: Reference Rajnesh v. Neha (2020) SCC OnLine SC 903 — Supreme Court framework requiring affidavits of assets and liabilities from both parties.
Interim maintenance: Available under proviso to S.144(1). Plead specifically.
Jurisdiction under S.145 BNSS: court of Magistrate where respondent is, or where applicant resides, or where parties last resided together.
Forum: Application is filed before Judicial Magistrate First Class. Family Court has concurrent jurisdiction where established.
Tone: factual, evidence-anchored. Avoid emotional excess; magistrates respond to documents.

sections.description: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents — where person of sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain
Interim maintenance and expenses pending disposal
Allowance payable from date of order or from date of application as court may direct
Enforcement — warrant for levying amount; imprisonment up to 1 month for non-payment per month
Bars to wife's claim — living in adultery, refusing without sufficient reason, mutual consent separation
Procedure — where application may be filed (territorial jurisdiction)

filing_checklist: Proof of respondent's income (salary slips, bank statements, ITRs, business records)
Proof of applicant's lack of income (no-income affidavit)
Affidavit of assets and liabilities (per Rajnesh v. Neha proforma)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: applicant_name and respondent_name must not be empty
amount_claimed_monthly must be > 0 and reasonable relative to respondent_income_monthly
If applicant_capacity is 'wife' or 'divorced_wife_not_remarried', marriage_date and marriage_place must not be empty
If interim_maintenance_sought is true, interim_amount must be > 0
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Rajnesh v. Neha (2020) SCC OnLine SC 903 — uniform framework for maintenance; affidavits of assets and liabilities mandatory; overlapping reliefs to be consolidated
Bhuwan Mohan Singh v. Meena (2015) 6 SCC 353 — Supreme Court emphasis on expeditious disposal of maintenance
Chaturbhuj v. Sita Bai (2008) 2 SCC 316 — interpretation of 'unable to maintain herself'
Captain Ramesh Chander Kaushal v. Veena Kaushal (1978) 4 SCC 70 — beneficial provision; liberal construction
Shamima Farooqui v. Shahid Khan (2015) 5 SCC 705 — Muslim wife eligible; provision is secular
disclaimer: Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.
